title: bug: JetBrains protected selection treats a UNC (network-share) spelling of the local project as outside it
description:
Objective: under the protected profile on Windows, JetBrains must not keep a PATH entry, or accept a node candidate, that names the local project through a network share. Found on 2026-10-30 while re-planning CQ-RF06b (task-032c973941bc41d9b051eedacb7de0b6).

Evidence (native Windows, architect probes):
- `\\localhost\C$\<project path>` and `\\127.0.0.1\C$\<project path>` name the local project through the loopback admin share.
- A JDK 17 probe shows Path.toRealPath keeps the UNC form (`\\localhost\C$\...\project`, startsWithProject=false).
- So RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject finds no project prefix in either form (normalize, toRealPath) and answers true, and MoeDaemonSupervisor.protectedPathEntries keeps the entry.
- With the same rule in VS Code, a bare-name spawn from an outside cwd ran a project executable through such an entry.
- select/installedExecutable accept a node candidate whose real path is UNC the same way. A mapped network drive that targets such a share resolves to UNC too.
- JetBrains already refuses trailing-dot spellings, because toRealPath applies GetFullPathName. Only the UNC part applies here.

Deliverable: on a Windows host, RuntimeSelectionPolicy treats any UNC form (spelling or real path: \\server\share, //server/share, \\?\UNC\, \\.\UNC\) as not provably outside the project.
- isOutsideProject answers false, so the protected daemon PATH drops the entry.
- select refuses such a candidate with a named reason.
This mirrors the UNC part of CQ-RF06b's VS Code isWindowsAlias rule. Accepted cost: network-share PATH entries and a network node are not used under the protected profile.

Not in scope:
- VS Code (RF06b owns it).
- Trailing-dot spellings (already refused).
- Mapping a share back to its local path.
- Persistent state.
- Enabling verified-local.
Local drive-qualified spellings and \\?\C:\ device spellings, POSIX hosts and the legacy profile do not change.

Depends on task-0ef30f9f1c0f4211946a16324dc60921, which edits the same JetBrains PATH filter.

Verification command: cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test. There is no Linux JDK, so from WSL run it as cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && gradlew.bat test". It must exit 0.
definitionOfDone: On a Windows host, RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject returns false for UNC spellings (\\srv\sh\x, //srv/sh/x, \\?\UNC\srv\sh\x) and for a path whose real path is UNC, and the protected daemon PATH drops such entries. Shown by new JetBrains unit tests that need no network access.
On a Windows host, a node candidate whose real path is UNC is refused with a named reason and no daemon is spawned. Shown by tests.
Local drive-qualified and \\?\C:\ device spellings, POSIX hosts and the legacy profile behave as before: the existing RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest and MoeDaemonSupervisorTest cases pass unchanged.
cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test exits 0 (from WSL: cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && gradlew.bat test"), with output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Windows: only drive-qualified forms are plainly local. Production change, one file: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt.

(a) Beside `defaultFoldCase` (line 187), add `internal val windowsHost: Boolean = System.getProperty("os.name").orEmpty().lowercase(Locale.ROOT).startsWith("windows")`. Use that same idiom; util must not call MoeDaemonSupervisor.isWindowsHost.

(b) Beside DRIVE_ROOT, add `private val LOCAL_DRIVE = Regex("^[A-Za-z]:/")` and `internal fun isPlainLocalPath(path: String, windows: Boolean = windowsHost): Boolean = !windows || LOCAL_DRIVE.containsMatchIn(comparablePath(path, false))`. Its KDoc must give the why:
- On a Windows host only a drive-qualified form is plainly local.
- A UNC form (`\\srv\sh`, `//srv/sh`, `\\?\UNC\…`, `\\.\UNC\…`) can reach any local folder through a share. A loopback admin share (`\\localhost\C$\<project>`) names the project itself.
- A device form (`\\.\Volume{…}\…`, `\\.\GLOBALROOT\…`) names a folder without its drive.
- Java's toRealPath keeps both forms, and nothing maps them back to the project, so neither is provably outside.
- comparablePath already turns `\\?\C:\` and `\\.\C:\` into `C:/`, so those stay plain.
- POSIX has neither form, so the answer there is always true.

(c) isOutsideProject: add a trailing parameter `resolve: (String) -> Path? = ::realPathOrNull`. Its KDoc: the real-path lookup, which tests substitute.
- Keep `candidate.isAbsolute`.
- Then require `isPlainLocalPath(candidate.normalize().toString())` BEFORE `resolve(path)` runs, using the `&&` short-circuit. A UNC or device PATH entry is then never contacted: no SMB connection, no NTLM handshake, no network timeout.
- Then every form in `listOfNotNull(candidate.normalize(), resolve(path))` must be plain local AND not within any project form. The project forms and the comparablePath/isWithin check stay as they are.
- Error handling is unchanged and fails closed: keep both catches, so Exception and IOError answer false.
- Update the KDoc: true only for an absolute path outside the project both as written and as its real path; on a Windows host both must also be plainly local.

(d) select: add as the FIRST when-branch `!isPlainLocalPath(real.toString()) -> rejected("$label is not a plain local Windows path", real)`.
- It goes before isRegularFile, so a share is not read again.
- The wording is the one VS Code's selectInstalledFile uses.
- rejected() logs the path and returns only the reason, as the other branches do.
- It covers installedExecutable (node) and installedArtifact (daemon, wrapper and proxy). A plugin installed on a share is not used, as with VS Code's network extension install.
- Do NOT pre-check installedExecutable's spelling. Its real path is checked here, and S8 reaches this branch through a device spelling.

No other production file changes. These consumers keep their signatures and inherit the rule:
- MoeDaemonSupervisor.protectedPathEntries, nodeOnProtectedPath and protectedDaemonEnvironment (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:566-588);
- protectedDaemonCommand (:515);
- TerminalAgentLauncher, through installedArtifact;
- ManagedVmPanel.kt:137-138;
- ProtectedStateStore.usableFor (:37). A state root on a share now reads as unusable, so state stays session-only: the fail-closed direction.
LEGACY never calls these functions.
implementationPlan.note: RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt only: added LOCAL_DRIVE regex, internal val windowsHost (same os.name idiom as defaultFoldCase), internal fun isPlainLocalPath(path, windows = windowsHost) = !windows || comparablePath(path,false) starts with a drive letter + '/'. isOutsideProject gains trailing resolve: (String) -> Path? = ::realPathOrNull; the spelling must be plain local (&& short-circuit) BEFORE resolve runs; then every form (normalized spelling, resolved real path) must be plain local and not within any project form. Both catches (Exception, IOError) kept. select gains first when-branch `!isPlainLocalPath(real) -> rejected("$label is not a plain local Windows path", real)`, before isRegularFile. Existing positional callers (protectedPathEntries, ProtectedStateStore.usableFor, tests) compile unchanged; installedArtifact/installedExecutable signatures unchanged. Compile is checked by the Windows gradle run in step 3 (no Linux JDK). Peer dirty paths (board JSONs, .moe/decisions, scripts/*, scripts/mods tsconfigs, docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) untouched. Open note: the inverse case (a UNC project BASE, comments on this task from governor-693b7073 and architect-6fc3dd5c) is not in this plan; filing it as a bug row.

implementationPlan.description:
Tests, one file: moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/util/RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest.kt. Change no existing row.

The paths below are runtime values; write them as Kotlin literals with doubled backslashes.
- Windows-only methods start with `assumeTrue("Windows path forms", RuntimeSelectionPolicy.windowsHost)`. They skip on Linux CI and must RUN on the Windows verification host.
- No row needs the network: every UNC or device spelling is refused before any lookup. The one exception is S8(iv), which touches only the local SMB server.

N5, isPlainLocalPath (any host, pure strings):
- With windows=true it answers false for `\\srv\sh\x`, `//srv/sh/x`, `\\?\UNC\srv\sh\x`, `\\.\UNC\srv\sh\x`, `\\localhost\C$\proj`, `\\127.0.0.1\C$\proj`, `\\.\Volume{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}\proj`, `\\.\GLOBALROOT\Device\Mup\localhost\C$\proj`, `C:`, `\proj` and `proj`.
- With windows=true it answers true for `C:\proj`, `c:/proj`, `C:\`, `\\?\C:\proj` and `\\.\C:\proj`.
- With windows=false it answers true for `//srv/sh/x`, `\\srv\sh\x` and `/w/proj`: POSIX is unchanged.

N6, isOutsideProject (Windows).
Setup:
- project = newFolder("project") and outside = newFolder("outside").
- A helper share(host, dir) returns `\\<host>\<drive>$\` followed by realFile(dir).path after `X:\`. assumeTrue that the real path is drive-qualified.
- `val untouched: (String) -> Path? = { throw AssertionError("looked up $it") }`. AssertionError is an Error, so isOutsideProject's error handling does not swallow it, and any lookup fails the test.
Each spelling below answers false both with resolve = untouched and with the default lookup:
- `\\srv\sh\x`, `//srv/sh/x`, `\\?\UNC\srv\sh\x` and `\\.\UNC\srv\sh\x`;
- `\\.\Volume{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}\x`;
- `\\.\GLOBALROOT\Device\Mup\localhost\<d>$\<project rest>`;
- share("localhost", project), share("127.0.0.1", project) and share("localhost", project) + `\bin`;
- share("localhost", outside). It is refused although it names an outside folder: the accepted cost.
Real path, with no I/O: isOutsideProject(outside.path, project.path, resolve = { Paths.get(share("localhost", outside)) }) is false. So is a resolve that returns Paths.get of the UNC string `\\srv\sh\outside`; Paths.get of a UNC string does no I/O.
Controls: the default call and resolve = { Paths.get(it).toRealPath() } both answer true for outside.path. So each refusal comes from the form alone.

S7, protected daemon PATH (Windows):
- As in S4, use supervisorFor(project, { null }, { null }).
- env PATH = outsideA, then every N6 spelling built for this project, then outsideB, joined with File.pathSeparator.
- After supervisor.protectedDaemonEnvironment(env, project.path), assertEquals(mapOf("PATH" to listOf(outsideA, outsideB).joinToString(File.pathSeparator)), env). The whole-map assert also shows nothing else changed.

S8, a node whose real path is not plain local spawns nothing (Windows).
Setup:
- Take (project, root, node) from protectedFixture().
- Add a helper volumeSpelling(file). It runs File(System.getenv("SystemRoot"), "System32\mountvol.exe") with `<X:>` and `/L` through ProcessBuilder, as junction() does with cmd.
- It trims the output and strictly matches the `\\?\Volume{GUID}\` line, then returns `\\.\Volume{GUID}\` followed by the real path after `X:\`.
- Java parses only the `\\.\` form, and toRealPath keeps it: a local device path, with no network.
- Error handling: on any failure it returns null. Guard with assumeTrue.
Assertions:
- (i) assertRejected on installedExecutable(volumeSpelling(node), project.path) gives exactly "node executable is not a plain local Windows path".
- (ii) installedArtifact(File(volumeSpelling(root)), "daemon/index.js", project.path) gives "installed daemon/index.js is not a plain local Windows path".
- (iii) For supervisorFor(project, { root }, { volumeNode }, started = started, statuses = statuses), ensureDaemonRunning() is false, started is empty, and selectionRefusal() is "Protected execution profile: node executable is not a plain local Windows path. Project and PATH copies of the Moe daemon are not used."
- (iv) share("localhost", node) has a UNC real path wherever the loopback share is reachable. It is always refused, and it gives the named reason when Files.isRegularFile(Paths.get(it)) holds.
- (v) Control: installedExecutable(node.path, project.path) is still Accepted(realFile(node)).

RED, then GREEN. Record both in the step note:
- Run the focused class once (`--tests com.moe.util.RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest`, unquoted) with isPlainLocalPath temporarily returning true. N5, N6, S7 and S8 must fail.
- Restore it. They must pass.

comments.author: governor-693b7073
comments.content:
@architect-4ae016fb Fact for your plan; the planner decides scope. On RF06b e83fef4c, qa-ba3f4f35 found the INVERSE UNC case on native Windows (comment-09feee65, 16:12Z). When the project/workspace base itself is a UNC spelling (\\localhost\C$\…\project, also 127.0.0.1), realpath keeps the UNC form. A local C:\…\project PATH entry then passes isOutsideProject, and a node physically inside the project is accepted. Repro: UNC_PROJECT_LEAKS=2.
This row's DoD covers UNC spellings of PATH entries and node candidates against a local project base. It does not say what happens when the project base is UNC. Java toRealPath keeps the UNC form too, so JetBrains likely has the same inverse gap. Check it before you submit. VS Code rev 2's rule is "refuse, never canonicalize", which would mean refusing a UNC project base under the protected profile. That keeps the IDEs in parity if you adopt it.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Under the protected profile on a Windows host, RuntimeSelectionPolicy treats any path form that is not drive-qualified as not provably outside the project. That covers:
- UNC forms: `\\srv\sh`, `//srv/sh`, `\\?\UNC\…` and `\\.\UNC\…`;
- device forms: `\\.\Volume{…}\…` and `\\.\GLOBALROOT\…`;
in the spelling or in the real path.
isOutsideProject answers false for such a path and never looks the spelling up, so the protected daemon PATH drops it.
select refuses a node, daemon, wrapper or proxy whose real path has such a form, with "<label> is not a plain local Windows path", and nothing is spawned.
POSIX hosts, drive-qualified spellings and the legacy profile are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: On Windows, isOutsideProject is false for `\\srv\sh\x`, `//srv/sh/x`, `\\?\UNC\srv\sh\x`, `\\.\UNC\srv\sh\x`, the loopback-share spelling of the project and a device spelling, without any lookup. It is also false for a plain spelling whose real path is UNC.
On Windows, protectedDaemonEnvironment keeps only the local outside entries.
On Windows, a node whose real path is not plain local is refused with 'node executable is not a plain local Windows path', and nothing is spawned.
The existing RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest and MoeDaemonSupervisorTest rows pass unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) A UNC-only denylist, as VS Code's isWindowsAlias uses. Rejected:
- On native Windows (architect probe, D:\arch-526a-probe\spawn.cjs), bare-name spawns also ran the project's exe through device forms (`\\.\Volume{GUID}\…` and `\\.\GLOBALROOT\Device\Mup\…`).
- Java toRealPath keeps those forms (UncProbe.java), so a `//` test misses them. A drive-qualified allowlist refuses both with the same one-liner.
- VS Code needs no change: Node's realpath.native resolves device forms to the drive path (subst-node.cjs).
(2) Canonicalize a share back to a local path. Rejected: localhost, 127/8, the host name, its FQDN, NIC IPs and DFS all alias the same machine (mem:decision-protected-windows-alias-refusal).
(3) File identity through Files.isSameFile. It is true for every alias probed, subst included, but it opens handles: it contacts shares and costs a lookup per ancestor. Deferred to task-1c2bfeca for drive letters, where spelling cannot help.
(4) Also pre-check the node spelling in installedExecutable. Rejected: select's real-path check covers it, and S8 needs a device spelling to reach that branch.
(5) Linux rows with windows=true for isOutsideProject. Not possible: on POSIX no drive spelling is absolute, so the real-path branch can only run on Windows. Hence the resolve seam.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Java on Windows (JDK 17, probed):
- Paths.get throws InvalidPathException for every `\\?\…` spelling (illegal '?') and for `\\.\C:\…` (illegal ':'). Those already answer false.
- `\\srv\sh`, `//srv/sh`, `\\.\UNC\…`, `\\.\Volume{…}\…` and `\\.\GLOBALROOT\…` parse as absolute.
- toRealPath keeps UNC and `\\.\Volume` forms. It calls GetFinalPathNameByHandle only at a reparse point, which is also why a subst drive stays `Q:\`.
comparablePath:
- It maps `\\.\UNC\x` and `\\?\UNC\x` to `//x`.
- It strips `\\.\` from device forms, giving `Volume{…}/…`.
Seams in RuntimeSelectionPolicy are defaulted function parameters (verifyProvenance's facts, foldCase) and internal vars reset by resetForTest.
The test helpers protectedFixture, supervisorFor, assertRejected, realFile and symlink (with its junction() cmd fallback) already exist.
This host:
- has no symlink privilege;
- runs mountvol unelevated;
- can reach \\localhost\C$.
JetBrains CI runs gradle only on ubuntu. The Windows rows run in the Windows verification command, which QA re-runs.
planningNotes.risks:
- A worker who resolves before the spelling check contacts \\srv over SMB, which is slow and leaks an NTLM handshake. N6's untouched resolver catches this.
- Never assert that a share is reachable; assert refusal only. S8(iv) asserts the named reason only when the loopback file is readable.
- mountvol prints `\\?\Volume{GUID}\` with leading spaces: trim it and match strictly.
- Accepted cost under the protected profile on Windows:
  - PATH entries on shares or device paths are not used;
  - neither is a node or plugin install on a share or device path;
  - a protected state root on a share is unusable, so state stays session-only.
  RF07 (task-f3f364a6) docs should state this.
- Out of scope: subst and mapped drive letters (task-1c2bfeca).
